decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm mouse approach: lift and gradually pitch the open gripper down, preserving elbow-up continuity. Mouse geometry estimated from current RGB.
Align the right gripper over the red mouse and descend gradually, rotating toward a vertical grasp; leave open until visual alignment is checked.
Close around the visually aligned mouse, then make a short test lift. Retention will be judged from the next images.
Mouse did not clearly rise on the first lift. Reopen and shift the grasp forward and slightly left to engage its middle rather than its rear edge.
Recenter the mouse laterally between the visible jaws, close, and lift 3.4 cm to check retention before transferring to the pad.
Mouse remains on the table. Reapproach lower and slightly back using head-view alignment; keep jaws open while correcting the uncertain fingertip offset.
Fine lateral alignment at the lower grasp height, then close and test lift the mouse while maintaining the same wrist orientation.
Mouse appears between the jaws after closure. Lift and transfer partway toward the pad, keeping the grasp closed and watching for retention.
Retention is now visible. Move the held mouse to the pad center and lower to placement height without opening yet.
Release the mouse on the pad, retract the right arm, and begin positioning both arms for a gentle keyboard push. Keep separate left/right workspaces.
Position the left closed gripper behind the keyboard while the right arm retracts clear of the pad. Use small descent and wrist changes to preserve the elbow-up branch.
Bring both closed grippers to the keyboard's near edge at matched height. Keep the push points on their own sides and avoid touching the clock.
Advance the two closed grippers gently against the keyboard's front edge, nudging it forward and right toward the outlined frame; check sliding and yaw from RGB.
The keyboard did not slide; the tips appear too high. Back off from its near edge and lower both push points about three centimeters before retrying.
Contact appears on top of the keys rather than the front edge. Retreat farther with a slight lift, then lower outside the keyboard footprint for an edge push.
Lower the clear push points slightly, then advance both equally to engage the keyboard edge rather than the keys. Check actual keyboard motion before continuing.
Keyboard is sliding now. Continue a slow diagonal forward-right push toward the frame while keeping both push points at the successful contact height.
Keyboard is forward but still left of the frame. Withdraw the right hand and reposition the left outside its left edge for a controlled sideways correction.
Set the left tip against the keyboard's left side and nudge right to center it in the frame. The right arm stays clear; monitor yaw and nearby figurine.
Make a final small rightward keyboard adjustment, then disengage sideways and lift with the gripper open. Next inspect centering before moving to the figurine and clock.
Keyboard is approximately centered in the frame. Lift away and approach the alarm clock from above with the left arm; retract the right arm clear of the organized mouse.
Use the wrist view to shift the open left gripper onto the clock rather than its right edge, and descend cautiously. Return the empty right arm toward its origin.
Clock is still left of the jaw center. Lift clear, shift left slightly, then lower the open jaws around its sides rather than pressing its top.
Close the centered left jaws around the clock and make a short vertical lift to verify retention before moving to the drawer.
Clock is visibly retained. Raise it toward drawer-top clearance with a slight forward-left motion, maintaining the closed grip and current arm branch.
Raise the retained clock above the drawer lip before translating onto its top. Use small increments at this higher, more folded elbow-up posture.

The upward continuation was rejected near a folded-arm limit. Replan from the executed pose: translate forward with minimal rise and gently reduce wrist pitch to clear the drawer lip without further elbow folding.
Forward motion also approached the same IK limit. Lower the wrist slightly and pitch the held clock forward without translating, to unfold within the current elbow-up configuration.
No motion executed in the prior attempt. Retry the same unfolding direction at one-quarter increments to satisfy joint continuity near the singular posture.

The small retreat restored joint margin. Swing the retained clock forward and upward by reducing wrist pitch, with only slight forward translation, to clear the drawer top without raising the elbow further.
Clock remains visibly retained but its base is near the front lip. Move slowly up and forward over the drawer surface with the now less-folded wrist configuration.
Upward motion reached the continuity limit again. From the actual pose, lower the EE slightly while rotating the held clock upward and forward over the lip, reducing elbow fold.
Clock is now over the drawer top. Lower gently onto the surface, open the left gripper, and pause to observe whether it remains supported.
Clock is released and supported on the drawer. Withdraw the empty left hand away from it, then prepare an overhead approach to the tipped figurine without crossing the arms.
The clock shifted off the top during withdrawal, so placement was not secure. Reclose and make a small recovery lift before attempting a deeper placement and a vertical disengagement.
Clock has fallen onto the table and is not retained. Reapproach its new position with open jaws and a downward wrist, using the observed displacement rather than the previous placement target.
Center the fallen clock in the wrist view and lower open jaws slowly around its sides. Keep the empty right arm stationary.
Descent is obstructed near the drawer. Back away from its front while reducing wrist pitch, then approach the clock with the forearm clear rather than forcing the blocked target.
With the forearm clear, make a small centering descent, close on the clock, and test retention with a short lift.
The clock slipped outside the left jaw. Reopen, shift farther left to straddle its full width, lower slightly, and retry a short grasp test.
The clock shifted to the other side during closure. Recenter slightly right and engage lower on its sidewalls before closing, rather than squeezing its upper edge.
Clock now appears centered between both jaws. Test retention with a controlled vertical lift, maintaining the closed command.
Clock was not retained. Reopen and descend with a more vertical approach, aiming for its lower sidewalls rather than its upper edge.
Lower another 1.8 cm around the centered clock, close gradually, then perform a very small lift to check whether the sidewall grasp holds.
Test the lower clock grasp with a slow vertical lift, keeping the jaws commanded closed and checking retention from RGB.
The clock still slips out during lifting. Move the open jaws farther forward and lower so their sidewalls engage the clock's middle, not just its rear edge.
Close around the clock at the corrected forward, lower engagement point and test with a four-centimeter lift.
The clock appears engaged at the deeper grasp. Lift and move left toward the drawer while easing wrist pitch, retaining a closed command and checking for slipping.
Clock retention is visible. Raise and align with the drawer while rotating the wrist toward horizontal to gain object clearance without excessive elbow folding.
Move the held clock deeper over the drawer instead of releasing at the lip. Keep EE height fixed and gently raise the clock with wrist rotation for clearance.
Clock is visibly well inside the drawer-top boundary. Lower slightly, fully open, and remain stationary to let it settle before disengaging.
Disengage from the released clock vertically before retreating. Keep the jaws fully open and inspect that the clock stays on the drawer.
Clock remains supported on the drawer. Move the empty left arm clear and toward the tipped figurine, angling the gripper inward while keeping the arm in its left workspace.
Approach the figurine from its left with open jaws, moving forward and down while keeping the left EE on its own side. Stop short for visual alignment around the stem and pot.
The pot is centered between the open jaws. Advance a short distance along the approach direction and close gently around its sides; verify engagement before lifting.
The pot appears between the jaws. Make a small lift and leftward transfer toward its stand, keeping the grip closed and checking actual retention.
The figurine did not lift. Reopen and approach lower and farther forward around the pot body rather than its upper edge, keeping the left EE left of center.
The pot is centered at the lower approach height. Close around its body, then lift a few centimeters to verify retention before moving toward the stand.
The figurine remains on the table and the closed tips were above the pot. Reopen and descend farther around the pot body, with only a small forward correction.
Advance the open jaws slightly along the pot approach and lower to its sidewalls, then close and test a small lift. The left EE stays left of center.
Check the latest figurine engagement with a slow lift and leftward motion toward the stand; retention is still uncertain from the small prior motion.
The figurine slipped and is still resting on the table. Correct the grasp height substantially downward toward the pot center, keeping jaws open and stopping above the tabletop.
At the corrected low height, advance the open fingers around the pot's middle, close, and perform a short test lift.
Figurine is visibly lifted with the pot between the jaws. Carry it left toward the stand and gradually rotate the tipped pot upright while maintaining grip.
The retained figurine is still sideways. Rotate about the world lateral axis to bring its stem upward, with a small leftward and downward correction toward the stand.
The previous rotation tipped the retained figurine farther sideways. Reverse that component and rotate back toward an upright stem, with slight lift and retreat for tabletop clearance.

The figurine slipped during rotation and is now beside the stand. Reopen and approach its pot at tabletop height using the new observed position; avoid further large rotations until retention is secure.
The pot is below and right of the current jaw center. Recenter backward-right at low height, close around the pot, and test with a short lift before attempting to stand it up.
The pot remains below the closed fingers. Reopen, back off slightly and lower around the pot body, then close and test lift without rotation.
The pot is engaged between the jaws. Lift and translate gently toward the stand without changing orientation, then check retention and placement alignment.
